subject: Re: Safeguard variance request — IDTA handover & TIA evidence
messages:
From: Anna Fisher <anna.fisher@medicorpx.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@medicorpx.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Safeguard variance request — Redwood DPA/IDTA

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start the procurement paperwork we ran into two operational constraints that require a limited variance from Redwood's standard DPA/IDTA flow. High level: MedicorpX needs (1) a 90-day request log retention window (instead of our reading of Redwood's default 30 days) for audit readiness, and (2) the ability to route processing for a subset of EU patient-data workloads to Azure Switzerland (CH) region due to local regulatory preferences.

We understand standard SCCs + UK IDTA/UK Addendum are Redwood's baseline, and we are not asking to replace them — instead we're requesting a documented variance and temporary operational handover plan for the two items above.

Attached is a proposed redline (proposed-idta-variance.docx) that sketches the language we're asking for and a short justification from our compliance team. Practical asks:
- List of subprocessors that would touch CH-region workloads and their attestations.
- Evidence that logs can be retained for 90 days (type and location of logs).
- Clarify whether KMS key custody options exist for EU-only keys (HSM/KMS integration).

We need to present a recommended approach to our Audit Committee by 2026-12-29. Can Redwood confirm feasibility and a target cadence for evidence handover?

Appreciate the help — copying Legal Ops for visibility.

Best,
Anna Fisher
Head of Privacy & Compliance
MedicorpX

Attachments: proposed-idta-variance.docx

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Short answer: we can work through this, but we'll need a scoped TIA/DTIA review and a subprocessors attestation for the CH routing.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood compliance will run a targeted TIA using our TIA_checklist.xlsx (attached) focused on the Switzerland routing and the extended logs retention.
2) Infra will confirm whether Azure CH (Zurich) can be used as a processing endpoint under our Private deployment options and whether KMS key separation is possible for EU-only keys.
3) Legal (Marissa) will review the proposed-idta-variance.docx and suggest contract language and any guardrails (timebox, audit rights).

Kimberly, can you confirm by EOD Friday whether we have a documented subprocessors list that includes Azure CH and whether we can produce attestations for third-party subprocessors?

Anna — we should be able to get an initial evidence packet (SOC2 + subprocessors list + short infra estate note) by 2026-12-22 if the CH routing is already permitted by underlying cloud provider agreements. If we need a code change or special routing policy that will push the timeline.

I've attached our public subprocessors list (redwood_subprocessors_2026-12.pdf) and the checklist so you can see what we'll validate. I'll ping you once Marissa confirms the contract approach.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Anna — looping in from Legal. Read the redline and Logan's plan; below are practical contract and evidence suggestions that will make this approvable without wholesale changes to our IDTA: 

Summary position (short): we can accept a timeboxed variance under the existing IDTA with these controls documented and accepted by both parties. Proposed controls to include in a variance schedule:
- Scope: variance applies only to workload tags labeled "CH-EU-PATIENTS" (customer-managed tagging) and is revocable with 30 days' notice.
- Retention: logs retention increased to 90 days for metadata and request traces only; full payload retention remains as per DPA (30 days).
- Subprocessor attestation: each subprocessor that will ever process CH workloads must provide a signed attestation (SOC2 or equivalent; encryption at rest and access control descriptions).
- KMS: customer may provide an EU-bound key with HSM-backed custody; Redwood to accept bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for those workloads where feasible.
- Audit: Redwood will provide an evidence packet (SOC2 report redacted, subprocessors list, network diagram, and TIA summary) via secured Drive link.

Evidence we will need from MedicorpX to close:
- Confirmation of exact workload tags and estimated QPS (so we can validate routing config).
- Regulatory justification memo (1 page) to include in the variance schedule.
- DocuSign counterparty details for the variance schedule and sign-off (I will prepare a short addendum).

Timelines:
- Redwood to provide draft variance addendum + evidence packet by 2026-12-22.
- MedicorpX to provide workload tagging + regulatory memo by 2026-12-28.
- Final sign-off target: 2027-01-05.

I attached a short summary (redwood_idta_summary.pdf) that outlines how we'll scope the variance. If MedicorpX prefers an alternative (for example, a longer retention window for certain log types), flag the item now so we can escalate with Security.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_idta_summary.pdf
